# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–5 (Complete and Final – Updated 66)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) just after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; Vauxhall evening during spring of first year; now spring of second year; narrative extends into future years; present day with Fred and Mary at Stone Court in white-haired placidity
- **Primary Locations**: Middlemarch, Lowick, Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton, Bilkley, Harrowgate, Melspring, Wilhaven, Salford; Also: Chiswick Mall (Miss Pinkerton's academy), Hammersmith, Soho, Thames, England, Oxford, Chiswick Church, Buxton, Kensington turnpike, Russell Square, London, Southampton Row, Vauxhall, Exeter 'Change, India (Boggley Wollah, Ramgunge, Budgebudge, Calcutta, Dumdum), Forty Thieves theatre, King's 14th regiment post, Highbury Barn, Covent Garden Market, Doctor Swishtail's Seminary, playground with tree and broken glass on wall, Bedford tavern, Thames Street (City), Royal Gardens, Quenwick (harbor town), Wilhaven (harbor town), St. George's Hanover Square, Lambeth Palace, Cheltenham, Great Gaunt Street, Queen's Crawley (Hants), Mudbury, Gaunt Square, Mansion House
- **Environmental Details**: Rain threatening; wind from water with salt and tar smell; gulls quarreling; smoke from chimneys lying flat over fields; frost silvering hedges; light going early; children chasing hoop down lane; road all ruts and puddles after thaw; somewhere dog barked then went quiet; river up in spring; muddy square

## Main Characters

**Dorothea and Will Ladislaw (Married)**
- Engaged after Will's return; now married with infant son; established pattern of two yearly visits to Grange; Dorothea's life mixed result of young, noble impulse; finely touched spirit with fine issues though not widely visible; full nature spent in channels with no great name; effect incalculably diffusive

**Mary Garth and Fred Garth (Married)**
- Inhabit Stone Court; seen in white-haired placidity at open window; solid mutual happiness; Fred becomes distinguished county farmer; produces work on "Cultivation of Green Crops and the Economy of Cattle-Feeding" winning agricultural meeting congratulations; Fred gradually saved enough to become Stone Court owner; three boys only, youngest resembles grandfather

**Rebecca Sharp (Miss Becky)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Age and Background**: Age nineteen; father was artist/drawing teacher at Miss Pinkerton's academy—clever, prone to debt and tavern, beat wife and daughter when drunk, died after third delirium tremens; mother was French opera-girl; claims descent from noble Entrechats family of Gascony; had dismal precocity of poverty
- **Appearance**: Small, slight, pale, sandy-haired with large, odd, attractive eyes; white slender fingers
- **Accomplishments**: Speaks French with purity and Parisian accent; skilled musician and linguist; clever artist; sings better than Amelia
- **Departure from Chiswick**: Threw Dixonary at Miss Jemima; obtained governess position with Sir Pitt Crawley's family after months-long battle to cancel indentures; Miss Pinkerton recommended her: "I cannot find fault with Miss Sharp's conduct except to myself; must allow her talents and accomplishments are of high order"
- **Calculated Nature**: Determined to make connected plans for future; never blushed since age eight when caught stealing jam; capable of calculated charm and intimacy; upon learning of Joseph Sedley's wealth, determined "If Mr. Joseph Sedley is rich and unmarried, why should I not marry him?"
- **Joseph Sedley Romance Campaign**: Invited by Amelia; won over entire household through charming behavior; left alone with Joseph in drawing-room; occupied knitting green silk purse; established great confidence and intimacy; Joseph began eloquent speech "O Miss Sharp, how--" but stopped when music ended; Joseph continued presenting nosegays; Rebecca refused his request to sing, citing low spirits; asked him to help finish green silk purse; Joseph seated tete-a-tete looking at her with killing expression, hands bound in web of green silk; Rebecca thought "I might go farther, and fare worse"
- **At Vauxhall**: Took Jos's arm as matter of course; sat by him on box of open carriage; everyone seemed to understand marriage was expected; lost themselves in solitary walk among five score other couples; situation felt extremely tender and critical; at panorama of Moscow, rude fellow treading on her foot caused her to fall back with shriek into Joseph's arms, increasing his tenderness; Joseph told her several favorite Indian stories again (sixth time); Joseph said "SHOULD you?" with most killing tenderness and was about to ask tender question when bell rang for fireworks; later in supper box during Joseph's inebriation, when Jos clasped her round waist shouting "Stop, my dearest diddle-diddle-darling," Rebecca started but could not get away her hand; laughter outside redoubled
- **After Vauxhall - Rejection and Departure**: Spent day after Vauxhall observing from little bed-room on second floor watching for Joseph's arrival; began feeling distrust and hatred toward George Osborne after he laughed and bantered her about her effect on Jos; feared Osborne had frightened Joseph away; heart beat quite quick; Jos never came all that day; received Jos's letter announcing his departure to Cheltenham and Scotland; Amelia's household turned against Rebecca; Blenkinsop reported Rebecca reading Mrs. Sedley's letters and accessing everyone's trinket boxes and drawers; Pinner suspected Rebecca had taken Amelia's white ribbing; entire household (except Amelia) agreed Rebecca should depart as speedily as possible
- **Departure from Sedley Household**: Accepted Amelia's generous presents with just proper degree of hesitation and reluctance; received purse from Mr. Sedley (willing to add twenty pounds more but carriage waited to take him to dinner); kissed Mr. Sedley's hand and asked permission to consider him her kind protector; behavior so affecting that Mr. Sedley blessed her and invited her to always come when in town; parting with Amelia theatrical—one person in earnest, other perfect performer; after tenderest caresses, pathetic tears, smelling-bottle, Rebecca vowed to love Amelia forever; Amelia wept confidentially on Blenkinsop's shoulder
- **New Position - Governess at Crawley**: Immediately upon departure from Sedley household, counted guineas from Mr. Sedley and began planning ahead; contemplated what a Baronet must be, wondered if he wore a star, imagined him in court suit with ruffles and powdered hair like Mr. Wroughton at Covent Garden; expected to be treated contemptuously but thought "at least, I shall be amongst GENTLEFOLKS, and not with vulgar city people"; fell to thinking of Russell Square friends with philosophical bitterness like fox regarding grapes; carriage passed through Gaunt Square into Great Gaunt Street and stopped at tall gloomy house between two other tall gloomy houses, each with hatchment over middle drawing-room window; shutters of first-floor windows closed, dining-room shutters partially open with blinds covered in old newspapers

**Joseph Sedley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Position and Background**: In East India Company's Civil Service; collector of Boggley Wollah for about eight years; caught liver complaint and returned to Europe; does not live with family but has own lodgings
- **Appearance and Habits**: Very stout, puffy man in buckskins and Hessian boots with immense neckcloths, red striped waistcoat, apple green coat with steel buttons; drives horses in Park, dines at fashionable taverns, frequents theatres and opera; extremely talkative in man's society
- **At Vauxhall**: Escorted Rebecca to dinner and through gardens; at supper, ordered waiters about with great majesty, made salad, uncorked Champagne, carved chickens, ate greater part of refreshments; insisted upon bowl of rack punch and drank entire contents; became inebriated, talked and laughed loudly, voluntarily sang in maudlin high key, became bold as lion, clasped Rebecca round waist shouting "Stop, my dearest diddle-diddle-darling"; continued to drink, make love, and sing
- **Post-Vauxhall Crisis**: George Osborne pushed Jos back into seat; Jos kissed hand to retreating ladies hiccupping "Bless you!"; seized Dobbin's hand weeping, confided he adored Rebecca, broke her heart, would marry her next morning; Dobbin shrewdly induced him to leave and conveyed him home; next morning Jos groaned in severe agonies; George Osborne found him groaning on sofa; Dobbin already in room tending patient; Jos's valet Mr. Brush reported Jos "uncommon wild," wanted to fight hackney-coachman, Captain brought him upstairs like babby
- **Escape and Flight**: Osborne mercilessly mocked Jos about Vauxhall behavior, called him milksop, mocked his maudlin state, ridicule about "my dearest diddle-diddle-darling"; sent letter to Amelia apologizing for Vauxhall conduct, attributing to rack punch, announcing immediate departure for Cheltenham and later Scotland for several months; thus avoided formal proposal entirely; Jos fled town, leaving Rebecca's hopes dashed and Osborne's interference effective
- **Father's Assessment**: Old Mr. Sedley has feeling akin to contempt for son; says Joseph is vain, selfish, lazy, effeminate; sure Joseph would say "Good Gad!" and eat dinner if family died; not anxious about him

**Miss Amelia Sedley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Character**: Pupil at Miss Pinkerton's; happy, handsome, seventeen years old; loves Rebecca like sister; natural infirmity of tears; match-maker at heart; too good, too kind, doesn't know the world
- **Betrothal**: Bred up for purpose of marrying George Osborne; banns read in respective families for ten years; appeared to fall in love with George at single instant when he asked her for music
- **Regarding Rebecca and Vauxhall Aftermath**: Discovered million of virtues in Rebecca; warmed into most tender friendship; shows her rooms, books, piano, dresses, necklaces, braces, laces; insisted Rebecca accept white cornelian and turquoise rings, sprigged muslin, white Cashmere shawl; entirely agreed with mother's changed opinion; thought Jos must propose next day; sent page to Jos's lodgings; reply through Mr. Brush was that master was ill in bed with doctor; believed he must come to-morrow but never had courage to speak to Rebecca; looked reprovingly at George when he laughed at Rebecca; after Jos left town, never had further word from him
- **Parting with Rebecca**: Ransacked all her drawers, cupboards, reticules, and gimcrack boxes to select presents for Rebecca; went to Papa to beg generous Mr. Sedley give his promised money (as many guineas as she was years old) to Rebecca instead; wept confidentially on Blenkinsop's shoulder about household suspicions regarding Rebecca; parting with Rebecca theatrical scene—one person in earnest, other perfect performer; after tenderest caresses and pathetic tears with smelling-bottle, vowed to love Rebecca forever

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Background**: Sedley's godson; family friend for twenty-three years; clever artist; bred up for purpose of marrying Amelia
- **At Vauxhall**: Paired with Amelia; at supper in mated pair; did not like rack punch; intervened with commotion, single push sent Jos back into seat; removed ladies in safety
- **Post-Vauxhall Campaign Against Rebecca-Jos Match**: Found Jos groaning next morning; not over well pleased that member of family into which he was marrying should make mesalliance with little nobody—little upstart governess; pursued advantage pitilessly; thought Jos milksop; mocked Jos relentlessly about behavior and romantic declarations; inspired feeling of distrust and hatred in Rebecca; laughed at her discomfited mien; when Rebecca came downstairs, continued liveliness and banter; told Amelia she must learn her station, called her helpless creature; said Amelia too good, too kind, doesn't know world; expressed manly compunction for unnecessary unkindness; his mockery and interference effectively discouraged Jos from pursuing proposal

**William Dobbin** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Background**: Son of merchant/grocer; father keeps shop "Figs & Rudge" on Thames Street, City; father became Alderman Dobbin, Colonel of City Light Horse, later knighted; Dobbin entered army
- **School Experience**: Giant amongst boys at Doctor Swishtail's Seminary, mercilessly bullied; defended George Osborne by fighting Cuff; thirteen-round fight where Dobbin, left-handed, eventually prevailed; character rose prodigiously in estimation; name "Figs" became respectable and popular
- **At Vauxhall and Post-Vauxhall**: Asked by George to look after shawls; carried Amelia's white cashmere shawl; paid at door for whole party; found himself humming Amelia's tune she sang on stairs; realized he was forgotten, decided he would be de trop; walked away; while walking about gardens, stepped up to supper box in agitated state when commotion seemed inevitable; shouldered off crowd; intervened with gentleman in top-boots
- **Jos's Departure**: Jos seized Dobbin's hand and confided secret of his loves; Dobbin shrewdly induced him to leave gardens and hastened him to Lambeth Palace; conveyed Jos into hackney-coach depositing him at his lodgings; next morning found Jos groaning on sofa, good-naturedly tended patient; entreated Osborne to have mercy when he mocked Jos
- **Emotional Attachment**: Found himself unconsciously humming Amelia's tune; emotional attachment to Amelia beginning to develop

**Sir Pitt Crawley, Baronet** [INTRODUCED]
- **Background and Ancestry**: Named after the great Commoner; son of Walpole Crawley, first Baronet, of Tape and Sealing-Wax Office in reign of George II (impeached for peculation); family tree includes John Churchill Crawley (named after celebrated military commander), Charles Stuart Barebones Crawley, and Queen Elizabeth's Crawley (represented with forked beard and armour in family portrait at Queen's Crawley)
- **Marriages and Children**: First married to Grizzel, sixth daughter of Mungo Binkie, Lord Binkie (cousin of Mr. Dundas); she brought him two sons—Pitt (named after heaven-born minister) and Rawdon Crawley (named from Prince of Wales's friend, whom George IV forgot); many years after Grizzel's demise, Sir Pitt led Rosa, daughter of Mr. G. Dawson of Mudbury, to altar; by Rosa he had two daughters for whom Rebecca Sharp now engaged as governess
- **Estate and Borough**: Owner of Queen's Crawley estate in Hants and Great Gaunt Street mansion in London; Queen's Crawley formerly erected by Queen Elizabeth after she was delighted with Hampshire beer presented by Crawley of the day; now "rotten borough" but Sir Pitt says "produces me a good fifteen hundred a year"; family represented in Parliament constantly for many years
- **First Appearance**: Rebecca's carriage arrived at tall gloomy house in Great Gaunt Street with closed shutters and hatchment overhead; door opened by man in drab breeches and gaiters, dirty old coat, foul old neckcloth, shining bald head, leering red face, twinkling grey eyes, mouth perpetually on grin

## Critical Events and Current Status
- **Vauxhall Evening and Aftermath**: Jos's inebriation and near-proposal followed by next-morning hangover and Osborne's merciless mockery effectively destroyed Rebecca's marriage scheme; Jos fled to Cheltenham and Scotland
- **Rebecca's Expulsion from Sedley Household**: Household turned against Rebecca on suspicion of theft and impropriety; Amelia innocently generous but house staff hostile; Mr. Sedley kindly provided purse of guineas; Amelia and Rebecca parted with theatrical emotion
- **Rebecca's New Position**: Accepted governess position with Sir Pitt Crawley's family; departed Russell Square contemplating her new genteel status; arrived at Crawley's gloomy Great Gaunt Street mansion

## Minor Characters and Details
- **Various Named Characters**: Mazek, Aessa, Ulvie Hollwood; Halan; Elnar; Jotho Corrett; others with minor appearances
- **Household Staff at Crawley**: John the groom; milk-boy who rang bell; man with red face, twinkling grey eyes, perpetually grinning who opened door
